outcome: Congenital malformations (gastrointestinal atresia or stenosis, renal agenesis, congenital heart defects, microcephaly, congenital hydrocephalus, other congenital malformations of the brain and spinal cord, diaphragmatic hernia, limb reductions, cleft lip or palate)
Recurrence of SUA in subsequent pregnancies
cohort: All 918,933 singleton pregnancies of > 16 weeks' gestation recorded in the Medical Birth Registry of Norway from 1999 to 2014.
finding: Single umbilical artery (SUA) was strongly associated with gastrointestinal atresia or stenosis, congenital heart defects, and trisomies 13 and 18, and also showed a two-fold increased risk of recurrence in subsequent pregnancies.
mod_finding: Previous Cesarean delivery was identified as a risk factor that increased the odds of having SUA.
